item: Intermediary-bank deductions on a standard (shared-cost) wire

why: HSBC China's CNY→USD customer rate was not retrieved, so HSBC totals show published fees only and the FX-margin cell is blank.

item: Receiving fees at US banks other than Chase
why: Only Chase's incoming-wire fee was confirmed on a Chase page. Check your own bank's fee schedule.

item: Wise: fees at other amounts, pay-out amount, discount schedule, overall limit
why: Five live quotes were read (CNY 66,763 to CNY 300,000). The recipient amount did not render, the monthly volume-discount schedule is not a published table, the overall limit is computed per customer, and whether a US bank charges for the incoming credit was not checked. Other amounts are not interpolated.

why: Bank of China publishes its own withdrawal fee; the network conversion rate and any surcharge of the ATM owner are shown only at the machine. Both cells are blank.

item: Current procedure for remitting home-sale proceeds
why: Order No. 3 Art. 22 says SAFE approval; a 2011 SAFE Q&A says the local SAFE branch reviews three documents; a 2019 SAFE Jiangxi Q&A excerpt says banks handle it directly under the 2017 capital-account guidelines. The 2024 guidelines (汇发〔2024〕12号) were not read in this session. Confirm the current desk procedure with the bank before selling.

item: Rental income of overseas individuals
why: Seen only as a search-result excerpt of a SAFE Jiangxi Q&A stating that such rent cannot be remitted; the item page was not opened. Treated as unverified.

item: Two official definitions of “domestic individual”
why: The State Council Regulation (Art. 52(2)) counts foreigners resident in China for one continuous year as domestic individuals; PBOC Order No. 3 (Art. 37) defines overseas individuals by passport, and banks classify by the ID shown at account opening (Art. 28). Ask the bank which category your account carries.

item: US–China treaty read only in part
why: Articles 1–11 were read. The saving clause, Articles 12–22 (gains, employment income, relief from double taxation) and the Protocol were not, and China's procedure for claiming the treaty rate was not retrieved.

why: The IRS page read names IRC §6039F(c) but states no percentage; the percentage cell is blank.

why: The regulation gives the maximum amount; the court decision on per-report counting was not re-read in this session.

why: Only Wise's FAQ was read: it describes the tax as applying to transfers sent from the US by cash, cheque or money order. The IRS release was not re-read, so the scope is unverified.

why: Only the individual income tax rule was read. VAT, surcharges, land VAT, stamp duty and the city's rate inside the 1%–3% band were not retrieved.

why: Notarisation and any taxes on selling inherited assets were not retrieved.

why: The Regulation allows conversion after liquidation and tax; the tax computation was not retrieved.

why: The two rate tables annexed to the Individual Income Tax Law are images on the official page; only the ranges stated in Art. 3 are quoted.

why: The tariff sets fees in CNY and does not say which rate converts a USD wire amount for the 1‰ commission. The model values CNY items at the board midpoint; the possible difference is bounded by the bid–ask width (0.42% of the fee).

why: Earlier editions list sending RMB out and converting offshore. The governing PBOC notice was not retrieved in this session; no steps or numbers are shown.

why: Notary fees, consular certification, translations and travel to file in person were not retrieved. Totals for the approval routes are transfer costs only.

why: The dividend is remitted by the company under its bank's corporate tariff, which was not retrieved. Only the withholding tax is computed.

item: Tax paperwork for an overseas individual's own large remittance
why: Guidelines Art. 59 require source documents including tax evidence; Art. 49(4) and Announcement 2013 No. 40 require a tax filing for single payments above USD 50,000, while Announcement 40 Art. 4 sends overseas individuals back to the individual FX rules. Which paper the desk asks for is the bank's call (Art. 68).
